claims.claim: The selected GET action is [HttpGet("{orderId}/retrySquareTransaction")]; it constructs RetryCustomerSquareTransactionQuery(orderId) and returns the handler call. The packet includes matching handler-injection and scoped-registration syntax plus a candidate Handle method, but Atlas leaves receiver and cross-file type bindings unresolved, so this is observed delegation syntax rather than a compiler- or runtime-confirmed binding.

In the candidate Handle body, the handler awaits CustomerCheckoutSupport.LoadOwnedOrderAsync(dbContext, currentUser, query.OrderUuid, cancellationToken) and assigns its result to order before checking Square configuration. If either Square AppId or CallbackUrl is blank, the body returns CustomerSquareRetryResponse(0, null, null, "Square is not configured in the new API.").

When those configuration values are present, the body computes cents from order.Total * 100, rounds midpoint values AwayFromZero, casts to int, and formats with invariant culture. It constructs payment data with that amount, USD, CallbackUrl + "/customer/callback", AppId as client_id, notes "OrderID:" plus the order UUID, and CREDIT_CARD as the supported tender; the complete data string is URI-escaped in the square-commerce-v1://payment/create deep link.

On the configured branch, the body calls CustomerSquareRetryResponse with success value 1, the deep link, and CustomerCheckoutSupport.ResolveHomepageLink(order.TourTimeSlot!.Tour!, _options). The included snippets do not show the response type declaration or establish any default error value; the resolver implementation and its fallback behavior are also outside this packet.
